title: Graph neural networks trained on a 2,352-compound screen find three selective senolytic compounds
summary: Wong et al. screened 2,352 compounds for senolytic activity in etoposide-induced senescence, trained graph neural networks on the results and scored more than 800,000 molecules. Three drug-like hits selectively killed senescent cells across senescence models with selectivity comparable to ABT-737; docking and TR-FRET suggest partial Bcl-2 inhibition. One compound, BRD-K56819078, reduced senescent-cell burden and senescence-associated gene expression in kidneys of aged mice. Evidence is from the abstract only; effect sizes, mouse numbers and the absence of efficacy or safety data in humans are not assessed here.

evidence.tested: Screening hits were tested in cell models of senescence, mechanism was probed by docking and TR-FRET, and one compound was tested in aged mice (per abstract).
evidence.unknown: Independent replication, human data and full Methods were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Graph neural networks trained on the experimental screen ranked more than 800,000 molecules, enriching for structurally diverse senolytic hits.

source_review.scope: abstract and bibliographic metadata (Europe PMC) only; Methods and full text not assessed
